newsitem.title: UK: AXA-UAP enlarges Sun Life in Britain.
newsitem.headline: AXA-UAP enlarges Sun Life in Britain.

text.p: Sun Life became Britain's third-largest life insurance company Wednesday after its French owner, the financial giant AXA-UAP group, restructured some of its British holdings.

Analysts said the restructuring, which had been rumoured for months, was to tie up loose ends left by last year's merger between AXA and UAP, which created the world's second-largest life insurance group.
They said it consolidated AXA-UAP's British interests and gave it a strong base.

"Combining Sun Life and AXA Equity & Law creates a powerful dynamic business at the centre of the financial services market," Sun Life Chairman Lord Douro said. "The enlarged group will be able to build on both companies' leading positions in a number of key markets and proven track records."

Sun Life & Provincial, which before the transactions was 60.2 percent owned by AXA-UAP, bought life insurance business AXA Equity & Law and AEL Investment Managers for a total of 690 million pounds ($1.1 billion), as well as AXA's British general insurance business AXA Insurance for 70 million pounds ($116 million).
Sun Life said it would issue 247.56 million new shares at 307 pence ($5.10) each to its parent to pay for the acquisitions, including 22.8 million shares for AXA Insurance.
The share issues will raise AXA-UAP's stake in Sun Life to 72.4 percent from 60.2 percent. Sun Life said it would have a market capitalisation of about 2.5 billion pounds ($4.2 billion).
AXA-UAP will end up owning 72.4 percent of Sun Life but has agreed to vote only a 65 percent share, and will cut its holding to that level by selling shares over an agreed timetable ending in 2000.

Sun Life said the deal would leave it with about 31 billion pounds ($50 billion) under management, enhance its earnings starting next year and produce cost savings of over 37 million pounds ($62 million) and one-time costs of 48 million pounds ($80 million) over three years.
These savings will be added to those due from cost-saving programmes already in place at both firms.
AXA merged with UAP at the end of last year and had total revenues of around 42.6 billion pounds ($70.8 million) last year.
Sun Life said Wednesday's deal would mean the enlarged group will get 84 percent of its income from its life assurance and pensions business.
